title: HEAT Letter: Zero-parameter redshift evolution of late-type galaxy sizes from a0(z) proportional to H(z)
description: Companion code and LaTeX source for the HEAT (Hubble-Emergent Acceleration Theory) letter. HEAT predicts the late-type size-redshift relation R(z)/R_0 = (1+z)^(-3/4) [Omega_m(z)/Omega_m(0)]^(1/4) at fixed baryonic mass from the scaling a0(z)/a0(0) = H(z)/H0. The headline observable is invariant under the proportionality constant; the conventional a0(0)=cH0/(2pi) anchor is used only for secondary absolute-normalisation tests. This release reproduces the manuscript figures and tables: the R(z)/R_0 normalisation curve, the stellar-mass-normalised compactification overlay, the ALMA z~4.5 kinematic cross-check, the BTFR zero-point diagnostic including the Jeanneau+2026 lensed-bTFR zero-evolution result, the SPARC local-anchor chi-squared comparison, the mass-selection mimic diagnostic, and the direct a0(z) / inferred dark-matter surface-density diagnostic against the MUSE-DARK trilogy. Current data are treated as consistency checks and challenges, not confirmation. Decisive tests require percent-level R(z)/R_0 over 0<z<3 from homogeneous Euclid/Roman-style samples and direct HI-based bTFR measurements at z~1. Included are the analysis scripts, Rotmod_LTG SPARC rotation-curve catalogue, heat_data provenance files, paper LaTeX source, reproducibility notes, and pre-generated figures under heat_output/. Licensing is split: code files are MIT; the paper, documentation, and generated figures are CC BY 4.0.
